tips.comment: Kamakameleon is a 2yo colt trained by Dylan Cunha. He is out of 2000 Guineas winner Kameko. The trainer won this race last year with Zminiature, and his entrant Kamakameleon is out of a dam that won at Leopardstown as a 2yo and placed in a Group 3 as a 2yo. The owners have had one other horse, a 2yo, that finished 3/20 in a valuable Harry's Goffs Million at York last year, with Sensorium bagging £61k. It's likely Kamakameleon is primed and ready on debut and is my short-priced banker of the day.

The Brockelsby can be a guessing game with all these being newcomers. At 60,000gns, NORMAN’S CAY is the highest-priced purchase in the field this year. He’s a colt by Sioux Nation who was a group winner over 5f and 6f. This 2-year-old is trainer Richard Hannon’s only runner in the race and only his third runner in this race since taking charge of the yard. His other two runners have finished first and third, with Persian Force winning for these owners (Amo Racing Limited) in 2022. Thirteen of the last sixteen winners in this race came home with an SP of 9.0 (8/1) or shorter. At the time of writing, only the top two in the market are shorter than that price, and the selection has attracted some early support. Market support closer to the off will be a more significant indication of this one’s chances, but it looks likely to go off as favourite and possibly at a shorter price than first offered.

4 places on offer for two year olds with no form so I think it should pay to side with a stable that targets this race and the Bill Turner stable has done well in this previously. Sire was a 112 rated Group level sprinter at 2yo.
Alive Haynes' yard has ready horses for debut and are having a good year so far. This one is drawn alongside the two principals and should make a race of it.

This is a large field of unraced 2 year olds so it's down to breeding and following the money. This horse is one of four for Roger Fell. He is bred for speed and has attracted support in the early betting exchanges.

Justice Twice can go well for the Kobeissi yard. Justice Twice has got a very good pedigree, and her mother won in France. I do not know this trainer, but this first-time-out filly is closely related to very good horses.
Not a race you would associate with the Holland yard. He has headgear on and has been gelded, so possibly today's the day to catch him.
First-time runner that is working well. If he doesn't need a run or two to be focused, he could run a very good race here. Good chance.

2yo not my forte, well nothing is at the moment to be honest, but AHEAD OF FASHION hails from a stable that have performed well above market expectancy in recent seasons. On that alone this debutant is probably worth a look at this price. He's this price because of the sire stats but still worth a play with the yard's credentials as an each-way return is very healthy.

Harswell Calling is another 2-year-old trained by Roger Fell in this race. On jockey bookings, this looks at first glance to be the stable's number one, but the odds are huge. The selection is speedily bred and can hopefully outrun its odds in a large field of unraced 2-year-olds.

Pressure's On is a 4-year-old gelding trained by Ed Dunlop. He is only 2/15 wins but seems to be progressing in his last two starts, having posted a career-high RPR of 86 in both his last starts. He made a seasonal reappearance at Wolverhampton, beaten a length behind Follow Your Heart, who is 10/51 wins, and Intervention, who finished 1 length behind in receipt of 7lb, won on Friday to frank the form. Pressure's On will strip fitter today on his second start after a 126-day break and has the capable Rossa Ryan on board. Off bottom weight and 9st 1lb, he should give us a big run for our money.

Naepoint returns in the 1:50 at Doncaster and brings a nice progressive profile to the table. He signed off last season with two wins over a straight mile at Redcar, showing he handles cut in the ground and has a turn of foot when it counts. He’s up in grade here but still looks fairly treated, and there’s a feeling he could have more to come. With a strong pace likely to suit, he’s one to take seriously.
Fitter than most, having won on AW last month. Unexposed sort who most certainly has his better days ahead of him. Has a decent each-way chance under a 5lb penalty here.

8/1 for PROMETHEAN with 6 places on offer seems decent value IMO. You could’ve hoped for a better draw (low numbers perform the best) but there looks to be a huge amount of speed coming from stalls 7 to 12 so there’s a huge possibility of a pace collapse on that side. It should set up nicely for a closer, such as Promethean, and his run over 10f here back in September suggests that he’ll be staying on strongly at the finish. D Menuisier’s 31% SR (A/E 1.39) with fancied runners when he’s got a couple at the meeting and 30% SR (A/E 1.25) with fancied runners carrying 9-4+ provides further confidence.
Formally trained by Aidan O'Brien, Ocean Of Dreams was sold for 32,000 gns and he is now trained in the UK by Archie Watson. He is having his first race for his new yard today and could go well.

Spirit Of Aklam might well prove an each way call here. The selection is drawn in eight here, and that should not pose a problem. He has won on similar ground in the past. He has cheekpieces put on for the first time and has had a break since a run in November.

Won this race last year from 1lb higher, so surely will be primed here for the repeat. Not disgraced from a higher mark last season, including 7th in the Cambridgeshire from 7lbs higher. Looks a great each-way price.
96 rated on the AW but runs here off 88. Could easily be better than that 88 mark. Romped home by 5L at Southwell last time out two weeks ago over a furlong shorter, so comes here in good form.

Myal from the Steph Hollinshead stable fits the profile of the type to run a big race here. The lightly raced 4-year-old son of Al Kazeem has won his last 4 from just 8 starts. The last win came over 7f on soft ground here back in October 24. Historically, 4-year-olds have won this race 10 times out of 13 since 2011. I like his draw in 10. He should be up with the pace, and David Allen knows this mile straight course well. Providing he stays the extra furlong, I am sweet on his chances here this afternoon.

I'm minded to go lower in the stalls for the Spring Mile and with the stable doing reputably well with the milers maybe FARASI LANE can outrun these odds. Has been kept warm with some decent looking all-weather runs so should be fully tuned up for this. Is lighter in the weights than when not missing out by much in an equally warm handicap at Sandown last summer, and returning jockey Kieran Shoemark was on board that day too.
Rhythm Master has not won since 2022, but was an eye-catcher at Southwell, when dwelling at the start, and running on well at the finish. Each way chance.

Empirestateofmind won a Class 2 Handicap when just getting up to win by a nose in a big field of 16 runners. He has yet to win since then (Oct 2024) but has put in some good efforts on the AW and returns to Doncaster where he has placed twice and was narrowly beaten on both occasions.
Thunder Roar has won at Doncaster before and was second in this consolation race to the Lincoln in 2024. Needs to recapture last year's form.

A seemingly wide-open Spring Mile, and a chance taken here on Rogue Encore, who found a jolt of improvement when switched to the AW with 3 good runs in quick succession in November with cheekpieces applied. Royal Zabeel puts real gloss on the form of his latest effort, given he is now rated 111 and didn’t beat this horse far receiving 2 lbs. The Rogue's horse has a bit to prove back on turf, but I’d be hopeful the retained cheekpieces can see him continue an upward curve and prove well handicapped off 84 towards the bottom of these weights. Hopefully, he can get a nice drag into the race by Naepoint despite not being drawn the best in a mid to high draw. The trainer has an in-form jockey booked who has 14 winners from 37 rides in March.

A progressive 4yo who has won or been placed in 9 of 14 races. Coming off a 4 month break but the yard is having a very good year so far and he should be ready. A good apprentice in the saddle whose 5lb claim is a big plus. The recent break and a gelding op could easily bring about more improvement.

Cynosure could be the one to provide quite a major upset here. Disappointing in the synthetic last time out, but on this track is likely to find better form. Good jockey-trainer combination and is better than that last run suggested.

James’s Delight was on a real upward curve last season, rising through the ranks and landing a Listed race in France. He wasn’t disgraced in a red-hot handicap at Ascot to finish the year either. If he’s tuned up for this, he’s got the class to lay down a serious challenge and could go close with a clear run.
Second in this race last season and comes into this on the back of three solid runs on the all-weather, so will not lack fitness.

This 4-year-old colt trained by Charles Hills showed some great promise as a 2-year-old, winning smartly at Doncaster in a G2 race. Since his wind surgery, he had an impressive win at Southwell over 6f where he definitely needed the prep run. Now he runs in a strong race but has a good chance.

Four wins and five places from just thirteen career starts. Not beaten far when finishing third on seasonal reappearance on the all-weather at Wolverhampton over seven furlongs three weeks ago. The drop back to six furlongs should suit and looks a value bet for each-way purposes with the benefit of that race.

Super consistent with three wins and four places from nine career starts. Only beaten by a short head last time out at Goodwood on testing ground. Has won first time out and looks the one to beat here with top young jockey Billy Loughnane taking the ride. Another positive.

Liberty Lane looked the real deal when winning the Cambridgeshire and backing it up with a strong second in a Group 3. He’s already got form at Donny and seems to thrive in big fields over this trip. If he’s tuned up for his return, he’s got every chance of landing another nice pot. Definitely one to keep onside.

The Roger Teal-trained, well-bred Camelot colt, Dancing Gemini, won a Listed Stakes over 7f here as a 2yo. He kicked off his 3yo campaign with an excellent ½-length second in the French 2000 Guineas. He then went unplaced in his next four races: three Group 1s and a Group 3. We know he goes well fresh (reportedly been working nicely at home), and a drop in grade should help on favorable ground. I am hoping he can get off to a winning campaign as a 4yo.

Group 2 winner Witch Hunter has a solid chance in what looks a highly competitive contest. He boasts plenty of strong form at Stakes level, and despite not winning last season, he was extremely consistent. He was narrowly denied in a Group 2 at Newbury and ran well behind the progressive Charyn on multiple occasions in Group 1 company. Proven over 7f to 1m, he finishes his races strongly and already has two all-weather runs under his belt this year, so he’s likely to be fitter than most. If the pace is strong, he’s exactly the type to pick up the pieces late on, making him a serious player.

Point Lynas has been a real battler in these big-field mile handicaps and looks set for another good run at Donny. He’s run some cracking races at York and wasn’t far off in a strong contest at Haydock last time out. He’s tough, consistent, and handles the hustle of races like this. Wouldn’t be a shock at all to see him right there at the finish.
Huge odds here, but with James Doyle booked for this ride and the finish LTO, I think Savvy Victory is worth taking on in this competitive field.

Class 4 winner at Newcastle in 2024 over this distance, but his OR should be nowhere near good enough to win a race like this. However, this is a new stable, and he wears a first-time tongue strap. Given this appears to be an ambitious race target, it hints that the stable might have spotted that the tongue strap has transformed him on the home gallops. Worth a small each way at 250/1.

Thunder Run is a 4-year-old gelding trained by K R Burke. He has 3 wins out of 6 and won a class 2 handicap off 96 at York, posting a career-high RPR of 104 over a mile. He handles today's good to soft ground. Sent off 7-2f under Ryan Moore at Ascot, he finished 4th out of 20 in the Balmoral Handicap, beaten by 3.25 lengths. He is clearly well thought of, behind horses rated 109, Witch Hunter, and the winner, the 104 rated Carrytheone. It wouldn't be a surprise if Thunder Run, a progressive horse, has the class to take this valuable prize under Clifford Lee.

The Lincoln is not a race to get heavily involved in with large fields, an unpredictable draw bias, and many of the runners having their first run of the season. However, one that ticks the boxes is Midnight Gun. The last 10 years have seen 8 of the 10 winners rated over 100. Since 2005, 4-year-olds have won it 9 times, and jockey James Doyle won this race twice in 2018 and 2019. The 4-year-old Kingman gelding has course form and will love the ground. I like the fact he has a middle draw, which gives James options. Not the biggest of odds but in my opinion, he does have a lot going for him.

Very consistent for Tony Martin and 13 days ago he won the Irish equivalent of today's Lincoln. Slightly surprised at his odds as the yard knows how to travel and plot a winner, and no surprise to see this one go close under a very good Rossa Ryan booking.

Whip Cracker shaped well on his seasonal return, finishing a strong fourth at Wolverhampton. Proven on various surfaces, he stays 1¼m and could improve further in this competitive handicap. Live contender.

Was 2nd in this race last year and was also a cracking 2nd in the Balmoral Handicap from 2 lbs lower. Relishes these types of races and goes well fresh. Only having 5th start for the Camacho stable, so there could be more improvement.
This one is returning from a break as it was a beaten favorite last time out with the same jockey on board. A good value each way bet for the 6 places available.

I've priced Native Warrior at 7/2, and they are offering 10/1. However, I believe the fitness concerns may hinder its chances. Nearly the whole field has fitness concerns as they are all going off very fresh. Ones that have had a run will have an advantage, but Native Warrior is a lot classier than its mark suggests.

Only out of the first four once in the last six outings. Has won a big field handicap over today's trip at Goodwood last season. Looks overpriced for each-way purposes with many bookies paying out on extra places.

Godwinson could go well if he’s tuned up. He had a mixed time of it last season but did manage to get his head in front, and he’s still lightly raced for his age. This sort of test should suit and if he’s ready to roll first time up, he might be able to sneak into the frame.

Sean is now an eight-year-old and has not won since he was trained and running in Italy in 2023. But after joining Jamie Osborne, he has spent his winters racing at Meydan in the UAE and placed in Group races in 2024. He was 4th twice in Group 2 races and a close 2nd of 16 in a handicap off his Lincoln mark of 102. He was also 2nd in an Ascot mile handicap last July off 106 and could go well in the Lincoln.
Two Tempting had a very successful 2024, winning five times. Had a pipe opener when fifth on the all-weather at Wolverhampton. Each way chance.
Seven places up for grabs and I could pick 7? I'll chance the Billy Loughnane ridden Oliver Show from gate 15. It should be fit now and looks underestimated.

Distance winner who finished staying on at the finish, 3rd of 8 on his last run in a class 2 at Goodwood on heavy ground. The run before last was a 2nd of 8 over 1m 37yds on soft (heavy in places). Both of those runs were off a rating of 92, off which he runs today but sits next to the bottom of the handicap, and today’s slightly better forecast going will suit. This will be the first run for a new trainer, so he has a new jockey on board.

Ran well in two top handicaps last season, including one at Royal Ascot. Been on all-weather lately and should have a fitness edge here today. A fast-run handicap could well be right up his street here today.
Apiarist has shown much improved form this winter. This all-weather form needs to be extended to the turf, and if doing so, the Lincoln could be on.

A lack of pace in here if you believe the pace maps, which does make it a bit more of a mess than it would otherwise be anyway. After much deliberation, I was minded to give Orne a swing on handicap debut here. His best form would have him well handicapped off 97 anyway, but with an added 5lb claim from Luke Catton, I thought an adjusted 92 was of real interest for one that should be forward enough. On the face of it, the trip is a question mark, as the horse's career has gone the wrong way over 6f. That said, he was a decent 2.5L 2nd when splitting two horses now rated 107 and 109 respectively off level weights over a mile at Chelmsford. Indeed, he's placed on 3 of 5 runs at the trip, and granted not got his head in front, but some of those were at the highest level so can be forgiven. Ground should be fine for him, and with him being just 1lb off bottom weight, hopefully that can see him home well.

Galeron returns to the Charlie Hills stable after a spell in Australia which saw him fail to get his nose in front in 12 starts down under. Returns to the UK and runs from a mark of 102, which on his previous form on these shores looks to give him every chance carrying top weight. A winner of the Winter Millions as a juvenile, he finished 4th in the Guineas before 5th in the Irish Guineas and 3rd in the Group 3 Thoroughbred Stakes at Goodwood. That form suggests he could be a 110 rated horse, and being in and around the pace (middle to high) everything looks set for a big run at a big price.

A very interesting looking class 5 maiden stakes race with my vote going to Kuredu King a highly promising gelded son of Churchill & Orcia ( Dam's sire the very smart Shamardal ) twice raced and showed good signs of promise on his first career start failed to build on that when last seen at Newcastle 142 days ago where finishing 10/12 however a line is best drawn over that as he had excuses on the occasion and he remains a good prospect for this season and is the type to do much better as a 3yo worth noting he cost 300,000 gns as a yearling stepping up in trip here a good move by his connections as it can bring out further in him jockey Kieren Shoemark takes the ride and can give John & Thady Gosden's inmate a promising ride here at Doncaster price at the time of writing looks of good value in my point of view and must be taken seriously and accordingly . Respected .

Providing Marioento handles running on turf, this could be his for the taking. He ran six times on the all-weather, and his last race of the season was by far his best when finishing first, having stepped up in trip. He races off a four-pound higher mark than that greatly improved run at Wolverhampton and will hopefully take another step forward over this slightly longer trip and win again.

LIFE ON THE ROCKS returns to the flat a full 12 lbs lighter than the last winning mark and has stepped up in form the last twice on the all-weather. So, it could be returning to the preferred surface at the perfect time.

Looks the best value in the race. I've priced it at 4/1, so taking this price is great each way value, especially for 5 places. It has a great chance at this mark and could run off with the race due to others around it having major concerns. It is a big field, so it may need a little luck in running to win the race, but I don't think there's any stopping it from getting into the frame.

With bookies paying 5 places, Life On The Rocks looks a solid each-way contender at double-digit odds. His handicap mark has tumbled after a long dry spell, but his last two all-weather runs in March suggest a return to form, particularly his neck-second at Newcastle just four days ago over today's trip. Now almost a stone lower than his last winning mark, he looks well-handicapped if this race doesn’t come too soon. Proven on turf, with four wins over this distance last season, he should be poised for another big run. The booking of talented claimer Warren Fentiman who claims 3lb at this level adds further appeal.

Placed on both of the last two starts on the all-weather over longer trips. Has run well on easier ground, and with the drop in trip likely to suit, looks a big price for each-way betting with many bookies paying out on extra places.

DESTINADO won over C&D around this time two years ago and could go well at a price in a re-applied visor with an in form apprentice, Mason Paetel (Last 14 days: 2-5,40%), taking a useful 7lb off his back. The selection runs off a mark of 66 but has won off a 3lb higher mark in the past. The 7 year old gelding has had a couple of recent spins on the All-Weather so fitness shouldn't be a problem while the James Owens yard is in form (Last 14 days: 5-28, 18%). He has a good draw in stall 6 and might not be the worst 22/1 shot you ever backed.

Monterio was sent off as a 10/1 shot when last seen here on the flat in this grade. So to be this price on his return here sticks out a bit. He could get involved if running to the form of the back end of last season, when showing some spark in trips at Sandown and Nottingham. Hurdle outing last time out, albeit a forgetful one, has hopefully served to tune him up.

A very open-looking handicap where the lightly raced Muhib can step up to the mark off a lowly looking 59 mark. His only 2 runs in handicaps have been full of promise, and he looks sure to see out this trip. 20/1 looks a big price in a weak-looking affair.

I think this horse will put in an 'all or nothing' type performance here, and I'll just take a swing on a small stakes win bet for that reason. He's clearly got no chance on recent form since he switched stables from the Andrew Balding yard, but the new stable are experts at racing horses off attractive marks. By racing the horse at AW courses that he doesn't act well around, they have got the horse dropped by a stone. Last summer, he was runner-up in a turf race off an 18lb higher mark, and the canny trainer has booked a jockey here to take 5lb off, who is posting some excellent stats. So I'm hoping this horse can bounce back on his return to turf, the first since he switched yards.

The first day of the flat turf is always a puzzle, but I am going for one that at least comes here fit from hurdling. Miners Gamble does have flat form here, having finished 3rd of 13 last October over today's trip. That was off a mark of 63, and with a 7lb claim today, he can go off an eye-catching 56.

Phone Tag appears as one of the more interesting contenders, just my opinion though. Hasn't had too much racing just lately so should have more to offer this season, wasn't quite at best form on the AW surface last time but turf may be more suitable and he may well have a fair bit more to offer on turf. It's not a bad draw , trip and ground conditions look to be ideal. At least an eachway contender in my view.

This horse has been placed on both his runs at this course, and I like the jockey booking in this Apprentice race. The trainer has had 3 runners in March and 2 of them have won despite him not being prolific so this one could be worthy of e/w interest at a generous 28/1. Last Summer he won over the same trip and ground as he gets here off 62 and he races now off just 61. Those course placed efforts were off 56 and 67 so he could well outrun his odds here.
Has to bounce back from a poor run at Wincanton last time out, but that might be possible. Takes a drop in class here and gets weight from all, which might just be the key.
Has come right back to form with a runner-up followed by a narrow win. Only up five pounds for that and should be very competitive again today.

Kayce Dutton is due a change of luck following a couple of runs in which being hampered by fallers, etc., more or less finished his chances. Confidence is tempered somewhat as the Pogsons' 7yo has to prove himself away from Huntingdon, so a small bet is advised.

Won at Kempton as a 2 year old and highly tried since, opened last season in the derby which shows the stable think highly of Kamboo. Looks a real dark horse and early season could be profitable for a stable in form.
Fitness and trip should not be an issue here, and possibly there's more improvement to be had at this trip. Murphy is a plus and will go close.

Previous winner over today's course and distance. Denied a clear run late on when finishing third at Lingfield last time out. Looks to have strong claims of landing a place at least here, with Silvestre De Sousa taking the ride a big positive.

Metier’s back on the flat at Kempton over 2 miles, and while he’s better known over hurdles, he’s got some solid staying form to his name. He’s been a bit quiet lately but could bounce back, and with Saffie Osborne back on board, there’s a bit to like here. Wouldn’t be shocked if he got involved.

The Alan King-trained dual performer Tritonic is not a horse to fully trust, but today the 8-year-old Sea The Moon gelding has conditions in his favor, despite being a 20/1 shot. He has course form, is down to a nice mark of 92, and has won in this grade. Worth a small each-way play at a nice price.

Balding is currently at a 21% strike rate. He won at this level at Ascot last season under Haley with Burdett Road back in 5th. He was beaten the next time in the Old Rowley Cup when conceding 12 lbs to the winner Sun God, 4 lengths back to 3rd. He travelled into that unbelievably well, and it'll probably turn out the winner was very well weighted there. Dropping back to 1m3f is possibly a good move too, and he has to be the one to side with here.

Unbeaten in two 12f handicap starts here, winning impressively both times, and is back to just 1lb higher than the last winning mark here in January 2024. Seems to prefer this surface but was not disgraced last year on turf, especially when 8th in the Coral Handicap at Goodwood from 4lbs higher. Sure to be primed for this.

Winner of both of the last two starts, including when battling on well to take the spoils over today's course and distance last time out. Could be difficult to get by if hitting the front turning in and looks a solid selection for each way betting with some bookies paying out on extra places.

Unexposed 4yo. Four career runs, form 2213. Two narrow defeats at this track to start his career. A 9L turf maiden win on his third start. Posted a good RPR rating when last seen, which was a decent class 2 turf handicap. Nice mark, 7 months off the track but could have a decent future.
Max Mayhem can go well for the Kobeissi yard. Max Mayhem has won in this race two years ago and is back after winning in Meydan two weeks ago. Can go well again at Kempton Park.

Killybegs Warrior is set to run in the 2:40 at Kempton. He has shown promise on all-weather surfaces, notably finishing second in this very race last year. With a current rating of 92, he’s well-handicapped and could be competitive if he recaptures his best form.

Mount Atlas has to be opposed here given Masar’s 1/10 record (A/E 0.2) with favourites over middle-distance trips and general 12% SR (A/E 0.25) with favs on the AW. O Murphy’s 11% SR (A/E 0.43) on Lope De Vega progeny makes Teumessias Fox hard to back, meanwhile Calumet has got a sizeable absence to overcome. C Bishop holds an awful 1/74 record (A/E 0.18) on horses wearing the hood which puts Balmacara up against it, but GREY CUBAN absolutely demolished the field on seasonal appearance last season (8l at Wolvo) so looks decent value at 11/1 (4 places). The gelding by Havana Grey won four from nine last year, the most notable being a C2 handicap at Doncaster in September. His run in the Old Rowley Cup was too bad to be true, only beating one home, and this looks a much more winnable prospect for the 4yo. H Palmer’s 23% SR (A/E 1.28) in 4yo+ races on the AW is another string to the bow.

Lieber Power has some decent form in the book from last year, picking up wins at York and Chepstow and going close a couple more times after that. He’s been off since the autumn but if he’s ready to roll, this sort of trip suits him well. Definitely has the ability to make a splash if he’s sharp after the break.

Veteran who showed he's still capable of very solid form when 2nd over course and distance in November and at Wolverhampton when last seen on Boxing Day. Should be in the mix once again this afternoon.

It's hard to know if horses are fully fit in these types of races, but this isn't a strong race. This horse turned into a proven group performer last season, winning a Group 3 and the Sandringham at Royal Ascot, and was then 3rd in a Group 1. Disappointing on last start, but that was the end of a long season. The fact William Buick is booked says she should be ready to roll, and if so, should be shorter than this 10-11.

I want to take on Soprano first time up as she needed her first couple of runs last year before getting better and better, and she's had quite a bit of racing now. Shuwari was highly rated and a one-time Guineas hope before an injury saw her miss her Classic year. However, she's still just 3 lbs behind Soprano on ratings, and this doesn't look too tricky a contest to start her off. If she's going to take top order amongst the fillies, she should be winning or going very close in this, despite the absence, and her stable have been in good form recently with 2 winners from 7 runners (also 2x 2nds and 1x 3rd).

Rose Prick has shown progressive form and now steps into a Listed race with a strong chance. She has performed well over this course and distance, and the race conditions favor her running style. With a solid record at this level, she looks like a smart value bet.

Crimson Advocate is a real wildcard here stepping up massively in trip after doing all her racing over the minimum. She was a sharp two-year-old and even won at Royal Ascot but hasn’t really kicked on since. The mile trip is a big unknown but if she settles and stays, she’s got enough raw ability to make things interesting.
Might just be worth chancing on fitness alone and a small stakes each way on the improving P Attawater runner Muddy Mooy. Eddie Greaterex, who has ridden it for both wins, keeps the ride.

A few of these potentially just outclass the rest on ratings, but I was minded to take on Soprano at least, whose worst effort has come fresh on 2024 debut. Crimson Advocate probably doesn’t have that worry but has it to prove at the trip, and Shuwari has a huge break to overcome despite the fact she could be the classiest of the lot. That leaves fillies rated between 78 and 94 who shouldn’t be winning this in ratings, but I still thought Queen Of Atlantis could be a nice price to hit the frame. She chased home a now 104 rated Fair Point when last seen, who she had previously beaten, suggesting there could be some sort of scope in her to be plenty better than this mark. 3/5 on the AW and 5/7 a place at a mile or further, her ability to get further and a lack of pace could see her go well if she can get forward from a wide draw. Hutchinson is 4/6 a place on board, winning 3, so his presence is a positive.

Trained at Newmarket by Comrad Allen, Mercury Day is worth an each-way bet at odds of 100/1. To be fair, Comrad's camp is just looking for some black type for their stable flagship filly, and they would be ecstatic with just a 3rd place.

Bermuda Longtail’s been going the right way and looks a handy type. Ran a tidy second first time out then got the job done next go, both at Kempton. Now stepping up to a mile which should be fine the way she finishes her races. Loves the surface, clearly got a bit of talent, and looks like she’ll keep improving. Wouldn’t be surprised at all if she’s bang there again.
Not much form on offer, but it is good form and fair figures. Maybe a little early to know, but if this horse does well today, I doubt you will be seeing these kinds of odds for a while.
Undefeated in her two races American Gal arrives here today with plenty of promise. She is up in grade on her season return, however, at odds of 11/1 a chance can be taken with her.

This C Appleby trained 3-year-old gelding has won two races over seven furlongs at Wolverhampton and on good ground at Haydock. He returned to this country having run well in defeat in three Stakes races in America. Having been gelded since, and with W Buick doing the steering, he should find this a lot easier today.

Hawksbill’s shown he’s got a bit about him, winning nicely over a mile at Haydock and running a decent fourth in a Listed race after that. He’s clearly got some ability and if he’s tuned up for this, he could trouble the odds on fav.

This Jack Channon horse can continue the trainer's good run of form here. It has been an eye-catcher on the last two starts despite not winning. The tempo of this race is just what he wants, and I think this is a good value bet.

Amazonian Dream is a proper all-weather performer and knows how to get the job done over 6f. Always gives you a run for your money and clearly likes the surface. If he’s in the same sort of form, you’d have to think he’s going to be bang there again.

No course form here, but definitely over this distance. I've looked back on speed ratings from the last run, and Monsieur Beaulieu is in the mix with the favorites in this race. The danger to me looked like Harry, who is also at a price you'd usually back. But at 16s, I think Silvestre de Sousa can really put the work in here and get up.
Walbank’s been a bit up and down but there’s no doubt he’s got a bit of class. Bit of a mixed bag lately but if he’s on a going day he’s definitely got the pace to make an impact.

Java Raja heads to Kempton with a bit of promise. After a modest debut on heavy ground at Redcar, he showed marked improvement to win a 1m4f maiden at Wolverhampton. If he continues on this upward trajectory, he could be hard to beat here.
If this horse stays in this weaker field, then it will win. SDS on board to give hope, but there are big discrepancies in price on each platform. Worth an e/w at the price.

Aiming High comes into this flying after an easy win at Wolverhampton and looks like she’s in a great place right now. She’s going up in class here but the way she won last time suggests she’s more than ready for it.

The way things are going for me at the moment, ENTHUSED will probably finish fourth here! I just think we can rule out the last two runs, which were well off what his preferred distance is. Now he comes back to this surface from the same mark as when narrowly missing out at Lingfield over this distance in September. If the new headgear combination works, we could have a live one.
She seems in good heart at present and valued for more last time out. Ground conditions will be ideal and she will be hard to beat.
Doctor Kildare has some very useful form and should be good enough to take this race. The trainer remains in good form and the step up in trip should suit.

Comes here from the same mark as when finishing 2nd on handicap debut last time. The form of which looks very strong with both the winner and 3rd coming out and winning next time, remembering she beat the 3rd by 15 lengths. Strong fancy here.
Georgi Girl was the best hurdler of these few horses, and at 4/1, I am attracted to her today. As I am writing this, she has gone to 7/2. She is good value at the moment.
Beat MOONHUNTER by 5 lengths, who was not far behind HITITI COLOEURS, who won at Cheltenham. Back on good ground, can bounce back here.

Chase debutant. Given a mark of 112. He has some useful hurdling form to his name. He finished a decent 3rd behind Push The Button on hurdling debut. That horse is rated 135. He was then pitched into a Grade 2 next time out but finished a beaten 6th. He managed to get his head in front at Market Rasen, beating New Order comfortably. He's not shown anything in his 3 runs since. To be fair, it was always about chasing with this lad. He won 1 of his 2 point-to-point runs comfortably, beating Sound And Fury by a wide margin. That horse is rated 124 under rules, whereas this lad is only rated 112. If he can show that point-to-point form over fences, he's got plenty to give off this type of mark. The trainer does very well with his chase runners at this track. Profitable to back them blindly.
Showed a return to form last time out at the course. He goes up in trip here, goes down in class, and is on a handicap mark he can win off.
Was well backed on debut when a very promising 2nd at Hereford over today's trip. Should improve for that, and on better ground might go one better.

This looks like a potentially very informative bumper with a number of likely types on breeding, including Mr Jukebox and The Bluesmaster. But at the prices, I will have to have an each way bet on Mini Mario, who is by the sire of the moment, Blue Bresil, and is out of the high-class mare Marias Benefit, who won 8 races for this trainer up to Grade 2 standard.

Midnight Lion has another great chance here after an impressive run under Lauren Young last time out over C&D 9 days ago. Has previously beaten Federated and Without Compromise and the weight swing is still in Midnight Lion's favour with 7lb Lauren Young on board again. Has a nice draw and if he can break well, I can see him leading all the way to the finish.

Federated’s a handy sort who knows how to win and seems to love it round Newcastle. Got the job done here before, followed up at Kempton, then came back from a break with a solid second. Should come on for that run and looks like he’s ready to strike again.

Going up in class, Without Compromise is still very appealing here. Watching back the last run, this horse kept on finding, so I think a drop in trip will suit. With 3 runs at Newcastle and a place rate of 33%, I think Without Compromise will start finding that finish before the rest.

Bayenah shaped with promise on debut at Doncaster, finishing third in what looked a decent maiden. She travelled well for a long way that day and should come on plenty for the run. The switch to the all-weather looks no issue on pedigree, and she’s got Jim Crowley booked, which catches the eye. With natural improvement, she should go close, and the early market support looks justified.

Herkeios was below par at Wolverhampton last time but had previously run well in a pair of solid handicaps, including a close second at Southwell off this same mark of 65. That effort reads well in the context of this weaker contest. He’s proven over the trip, handles Tapeta, and returns to a straight mile which could play to his strengths. If he can recapture that Southwell form, he looks a leading player here and the early double-figure odds offer fair value.

La Botte ran a lot better than the market expected on debut at Kempton, staying on nicely for third over 7f. That looked a fair race and he shaped like one who’d come on plenty for it. Up to a mile now and with that experience under his belt, he should be sharper. Wouldn’t be surprised to see him go very close.

Tuco Salamanca has shown some encouraging signs in his recent runs. He has been settling well early on and then picking up the pace in the latter stages which suits Newcastle’s track conditions perfectly.

Saxonia looks like a strong prospect based on her recent form and the way she handles similar conditions. Her previous runs show she settles well early and then has a steady finish that can challenge the leaders in a competitive field. The current track conditions favor her running style and make her a horse worth considering today.
3rd to Tuco Salamanca 15 days ago when he gave 2 lbs, now 3 lbs better off. Improving since yard switch and now brought back slightly in trip, which should suit.

Oriental Prince is in great form and looks poised to lead the field. His strong early pace and powerful finishing ability have impressed, and today’s track conditions perfectly suit his running style.

This horse has been beaten a neck in his 2 recent runs over c&d off a 1lb lower mark. He traded very short odds on both occasions and was particularly unlucky in one of those races where Jonny Peate was on board and travelling like a dream before being hampered at a crucial time. That was his only ride on the horse and I like his booking here to make amends for that defeat. Looks sure to go very close here.
WYVERN just looks a big price for a horse that very nearly won earlier in the week. Grade and distance shouldn't be a problem despite changes to both and could win it from here.

Kings School is in excellent form and shows all the signs of being a real contender. His recent performances have been impressive, with a strong early pace followed by a powerful finish that has often put him ahead of the field. Today’s conditions are ideal for his running style, and he has the potential to outrun his odds.
